The Police Sub-Inspector of Sanjay Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 498A, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Pallavi was solemnized with accused on 12-12-2021 as per Hindu rite and customs.
At that time, the accused received one gold ring as dowry from CW3 and CW4.

After the marriage, CW1 resided with accused at house No. 105/3, 5 th Cross,
Geddalahalli, within the limits of Sanjay Nagara PS, Bengaluru, where accused started ill-treating CW1 for fetching of additional dowry amount from her parents to do finance business and received Rs.1,50,000/- from her CW3 and CW4.

On 28-03-2023 at 3.30 pm, accused picked up quarrel with CW1, beaten and abused her in filthiest language and threatened her with life consequences and subjected CW1 to mental and physical cruelty for fetching of additional dowry.
3. First Information Report:

Upon the receipt of first information from CW1, CW10 Sri Hareesh Kumar.J. the then PSI of Sanjay Nagar Police Station registered Crime No.71/2023 against the KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 accused for the offences punishable under Section 498A,
506, 506 of IPC and Sec.3, 4 of D.P. Act, prepared FIR sent the same to the Court and drawn spot mahazar on 01-04-2023 and handed over the case papers to CW11.

Pallavi vs Raghu on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144916254/
2

4. Investigation: Thereafter CW11 Sri Guruprasad.A., PI of Sanjay Nagara PS, continued the investigation, recorded the statement of witnesses, collected the documents and after completion of investigation, submitted charge sheet against the accused for the alleged offences.
5. The accused was enlarged on bail by the order dated 21-12-2023.
6. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court had taken cognizance for the offences alleged against the accused.
7. Copies of prosecution papers as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.

8. Charge: After hearing learned Senior APP and counsel for accused, charge for offences punishable U/Sec 498A, 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 Section 3,
4 of Dowry Prohibition Act has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 11 witnesses and examined 1 witnesses and exhibited 6 documents and closed their side.

The learned Senior APP prays for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as PW1 and the accused have compromised the matrimonial differences in M.C. No.4819/2023 and hence the examination of CW2 to CW11 was dispensed with by the order dated 04/12/2025.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences found against the accused from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
11.
Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Pallavi was solemnized with accused on 12-12-2021, at that time, the accused received one gold ring as dowry from CW3 and CW4 thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable under Sec.3 of D.P. Act?

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that after the marriage, CW1 resided with accused at house No.105/3, 5th Cross, Geddalahalli, within the limits of Sanjay Nagara PS, Bengaluru, where accused started ill-treating CW1 for fetching of additional dowry amount from her parents and subjected CW1 to mental and physical cruelty thereby resulted in commission of an KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 offence punishable under Sec.498(A) of IPC?

Pallavi vs Raghu on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144916254/
3 3.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said place and duration, the accused received Rs.1,50,000/- from CW3 and CW4 as additional dowry thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.4 of D.P. Act.?

4. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 28-03-2023 at 3.30 pm, at above said place, the accused abused CW1 in filthiest language thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.504 of IPC?
5.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on above said date, time and place, the accused had put life threat to CW1 thereby resulted in commission KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 of an offence punishable u/Sec.506 of IPC?
6. What order?

13. The findings on the above points are as under:
Point No.1 - 5 : In the Negative Point No.6 : As per final order REASONS 14. Point No.1 to 5: These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined CW1 by name Smt. Pallavi, being Informant as PW1 identified her signature on Ex.P1 (Complaint) and Ex.P2 (Spot Mahzar) as Ex.P1(a) and Ex.P2(a)
deposed that when she went to the police station for sorting out the differences of opinion amongst her and the accused, the police obtained her signature on the said document, she does not know the content of Ex.P1 and Ex. P. 2 and further deposed that she did not lodge any complaint against accused and she has not taken any treatment KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 with the history of assault.
In this regard, the learned Senior APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness however no favorable answers has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness however no favorable answer has been elicited from her to support the prosecution case.

Her denial of statement given before police is marked as per Ex.P3.
15.

However PW1 admitted in her chief examination as under           
 .  .

Mediation      

 ,    


 
  
 


   
 

 
   
 

 
 

     


 
   
  
   
    
   

      
    

 

   .2,00,000/-

. 
Pallavi vs Raghu on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144916254/
4 The certified copies of order sheet, Decree and Memorandum of Settlement in MC No.4819/2023 are marked as Ex.P4 to Ex.P6 respectively.

On KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 perusal of the above evidence, it appears that the disputes between the accused and PW1 (informant) have been resolved amicably and PW1 received Rs.2,00,000/- as permanent alimony and their marital relationship was ended in divorce.
16.

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana and anr in the case of AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. State of haryana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
and in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat),
wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

It further held that after examining the nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498(A), 504, 506 of IPC are the off- shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/PW1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

17. In the case of the KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464,
wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 18. Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
Under these circumstances, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.

Moreover the evidence of other Pallavi vs Raghu on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144916254/
5 witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned Sr.APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the ingredients for offences Under Section 498(A), 504, 506 of IPC was not proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answer the point No.1 to 5 in the Negative.
19. Point No.6:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 5, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
KABC030456312023 CC No.25872/2023 ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec. 498(A), 504, 506 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3, 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.
(iv) Ordered accordingly.
